extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and students of scientific method
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on kinds of experimental 'instances' (instruments, tests, and observations) for investigating natural natures — how to assist the senses, bring the insensible to view, distinguish natures, and infer hidden agents. Mostly drawn from Bacon's Novum Organum with editorial notes and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin investigation from the senses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cum enim omnis interpretatio naturae incipiat a sensu ... necesse est ut, quanto magis copiosae et exactae fuerint repraesentationes sive praebitiones ipsius sensus, tanto omnia cedant facilius et foelicius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of nature must start with the senses; procuring copious, exact, and well-provided sensory representations (via instruments/tests) makes intellectual perception and true notions easier to attain. Emphasizes strengthening and correcting sensory input before abstract reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances Lampadis (Informative Instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequuntur quinque ordines instantiarum, quas uno vocabulo generali Instantias Lampadis sive Informationis Primae appellare consuevimus. Eae sunt quae auxiliantur sensui.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five orders of instances serve to inform or supply defects of the senses; they collectively 'inform' the understanding by assisting sensory perception. Use them as a primary class of experimental aids when seeking true notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lampadis — Order I: strengthen/amplify/rectify immediate senses
rubrics_metrics.description: Harum autem quinque instantiarum Lampadis, primae roborant, ampliant, et rectificant actiones sensus immediatas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design or employ instances/instruments/tests whose direct effect is to correct, amplify, or make more reliable the immediate action of senses (e.g., optical aids when properly correcting vision). Prioritize improving raw sensory data before higher inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lampadis — Order II: deduce the non-sensible to the sensible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instances that make invisible or otherwise non-sensible phenomena manifest through sensible effects (e.g., devices or experimental setups that translate a hidden property into an observable mark). These are crucial for studying subtle or non-directly-perceptible natures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lampadis — Order III: indicate continuous processes/series
rubrics_metrics.description: Tertiae indicant processus continuatos sive series earum rerum et motuum quae (ut plurimum) non notantur nisi in exitu aut periodis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ instances that reveal processes or series of changes that would otherwise be noticed only by their outcomes or periodic appearances. Useful for reconstructing intermediate stages of motion or transformation (serial observations, long-run monitoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lampadis — Order IV: substitute for sense in cases of deprivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quartae aliquid substituunt sensui in meris destitutionibus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a sense is unavailable or inadequate, use instruments or tests that substitute for it (e.g., thermometers for temperature where direct tactile sense fails). These instances provide alternative avenues for obtaining necessary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lampadis — Order V: excite attention and bound subtility
rubrics_metrics.description: Quintaes excitant attentionem sensus et advertentiam, atque una limitant subtilitatem rerum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instances that draw attention to phenomena and restrict excessively subtle speculation by making salient distinctions. They help focus investigation on tractable differences rather than endless minute conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances Januae (Gates/Portals) — aids to immediate senses (especially vision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter praerogativas instantiarum ponemus loco decimo sexto Instantias Januae sive Portae: eo enim nomine eas appellamus quae juvant actiones sensus immediatas. Inter sensus autem manifestum est partes primas tenere Visum, quoad informationem; quare huic sensui praecipue auxilia conquirenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Januae are instruments or aids that assist immediate sensory perception, primarily sight. They are meant to enable seeing what is otherwise unseen, at greater distance, or with greater accuracy. Selecting the appropriate Januae is essential for observational work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Januae type I: instruments to perceive the unseen (perspicilla / microscopes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primi generis sunt ... ea quae nuper inventa sunt perspicilla; quae latentes et invisibiles corporum minutias ... demonstrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microscopes and similar instruments reveal minute and hidden structures (bodies, motions, colors) with enlarged species. Beware two anti-patterns: (1) using such instruments superstitionally to 'dishonor' nature; (2) overextending a tool that only reveals minutiae and thus destroying proper use. Instruments must be competent for the scale of phenomena studied; repeated, varied experiments and extension to useful scales are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Januae type II: instruments to extend vision at distance (telescopes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secundi generis sunt ilia altera perspicilla — quae memorabili conatu adinvenit Galilaeus; quorum ope, tanquam per scaphas aut naviculas, aperiri et exerceri possint propiora cum coelestibus commercia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telescopes extend sight to celestial distances, revealing new phenomena (satellites, solar spots, lunar markings). Use with caution: optical delusions are possible; discoveries require many corroborating observations rather than single reports. Instruments should be improved, tests repeated, and observers should openly report contrary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Januae type III: measuring/rectifying instruments (bacilla, astrolabe, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tertii generis sunt bacilla illa ad terras mensurandas, astrolabia, et similia; quae sensum videndi non ampliant, sed rectificant et dirigunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instruments do not magnify perception but provide measurement, correction, and direction (e.g., astrolabes, surveying rods). Use them to obtain precise positional or metric data; they rectify and guide sensory judgments and are essential where exactitude is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances Citantes / Evocantes (to bring the insensible before the senses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter praerogativas instantiarum ponemus loco decimo septimum Instantias Citantes, sumpto vocabulo a foris civilibus, quia citant ea ut compareant quae prius non comparuerunt; quasetiam Instantias Evocantes appellare consuevimus. Eae deducunt non-sensibile ad sensibile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citantes are experimental instances that 'cite' or bring formerly non-apparent phenomena within sensory reach by producing sensible indications. They are the class of tests/devices that make the insensible manifest through signs or secondary effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons why objects escape the senses (taxonomy of invisibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensum autem fugiunt res, vel propter distantiam objecti locati; vel propter interceptionem sensus per corpora media; vel quia objectum non est habile ad impressionem in sensu facicndam; vel quia deficit quantum in objecto pro feriendo sensu; vel quia tempus non est proportionatum ad actuandum sensum; vel quia objecti percussio non toleratur a sensu; vel quia objectum ante implevit et possedit sensum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing instances or experiments, consider the categorical reasons a phenomenon might evade perception (distance; intervening media; inability to impress the sense; insufficient magnitude; insufficient time; intolerable impact; prior occupation of the sense). Tailor methods to address the specific cause (e.g., extend range, remove media, amplify impression, prolong exposure, use indirect indicators).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citantes technique I: use substitutive signs to provoke distant perception
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) In primo genere non fit deductio ad sensibile, nisi rei, quae cerni non posit propter distantiam, adjiciatur aut substituatur alia res quae sensum magis e longinquo provocare et ferire possit: veluti in significatione rerum per ignes, campanas, et similia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distance prevents direct perception, create or use signs that can be perceived from afar (fires, bells, flags, remote indicators). This substitutes a detectable effect for the undetectable object and allows inference of the object's state or occurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citantes technique II: deduce hidden states from surface indications or effluvia
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) In secundo genere fit deductio, cum ea quae interius propter interpositionem corporum latent, nee commode aperiri possunt, per ea quae sunt in superficie, aut ab interioribus effluunt, perducuntur ad sensum: ut status humanorum corporum per pulsus, et urinas, et similia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infer internal or hidden conditions by observing surface manifestations or emitted products (pulse, urine, odors, effluvia). Use instruments (stethoscope, chemical tests) and established correlations to translate these surface signs into knowledge of internal states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citantes technique III/IV: use sensitive tests/indicators (thermometer, galvanic/actinic tests) to detect subtle changes
rubrics_metrics.description: (3, 4) ... exempla: thermometer, thermo-electric pile, tests for gases, experiments showing actinism — tests of all kinds fall under one or other of these heads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ sensitive instruments or indicator systems (thermometers, thermoelectric piles, chemical indicators, electrochemical setups) that reveal small or gradual changes imperceptible to unaided senses. These are essential for detecting minute additions, temperature shifts, chemical traces, or radiation effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferring hidden 'spirit' or internal agents from observable effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Sit itaque natura inquisita Actio et Motus Spiritus ... Spiritus enim in re tangibili, emissus, corpora contrahit et desiccat; detentus, corpora intenerat et colliquat; nee prorsus emissus nee prorsus detentus, informat, membrificat, assimilat, egerit, organizat, et similia. ... Etenim in omni corpore tangibili inanimato, spiritus inclusus primo multiplicat se ... Atque haec omnia deducuntur ad sensibile per effectus conspicuos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To infer internal agents (here called 'spirit') deduce from their observable effects: desiccation and weight loss, rust and putrefaction, contraction or swelling, formation of organic structures, and the appearance of 'animalcules' in putrefaction. Use controlled experiments that isolate variables (heating, confinement, observation of effluvia, microscopic examination) to relate observable changes to hypothesized internal forces. Note limitations: 'spirit' itself may not weigh; infer by correlated sensible changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish Januae (detect objects themselves) from Citantes (detect only indications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first and fourth of these cases are... Januae enable detection of the objects themselves provided instruments are sufficiently powerful, whereas Instantiae Citantes are for objects which cannot be known in themselves but only by means of indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing methods, decide whether you aim to observe the object directly (use Januae: more powerful instruments) or only to obtain signs of it (use Citantes: indirect indicators). This distinction guides instrument selection and experiment design and warns against conflating direct observation with inference from signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repeated, varied, and self-critical experimentation; beware one-off observations and optical delusions
rubrics_metrics.description: From editorial notes and examples: 'neque alia complura investigatu aeque digna eadem ratione inventa sint' and cautions about optical delusions — 'Galileo's discoveries were often represented as mere optical delusions' and advice: 'instrumenta mutent, et test.um numerum augeant, et singula et saepe experiantur, et varie; denique ut et sibi ipsi obiiciant et aliis patefaciant quid in contrarium objici possit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate observations by varying instruments and repeating experiments; increase the number of tests; subject results to severe criticism and expose them to attempts at refutation. Avoid trusting single observations or instruments without cross-checks.
